title: Impact of Income on Civil Conflict Using Rainfall Variation

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two-Stage Least Squares (Instrumental Variables).  
Why IV? Income (x) may be endogenous to conflict (y) because of reverse causality and omitted variables. Rainfall variation (z) affects agricultural income but, conditional on controls, plausibly affects conflict only through its effect on income.  

Key assumptions  
1. Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0 – rainfall shocks move income.  
2. Exclusion / Exogeneity: Rainfall affects conflict solely through income and is uncorrelated with the structural error in the conflict equation.  
3. Monotonicity (implicit with a single continuous instrument).  

## 2. R Code
```r
# -------------------- SET-UP -------------------- #
# Required packages
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(AER)        # ivreg
  library(sandwich)   # robust vcov
  library(lmtest)     # coeftest
})

# -------------------- DATA -------------------- #
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s70_data.csv")

# Ensure correct types
df$z <- as.numeric(df$z)          # instrument
df$controls <- as.numeric(df$controls)

# -------------------- MODELS -------------------- #
# OLS benchmark
ols_mod <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)

# IV: income instrumented by rainfall
iv_mod  <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df)

# -------------------- ROBUST INFERENCE -------------------- #
rob_se   <- function(model) vcovHC(model, type = "HC1")
ols_res  <- coeftest(ols_mod,  vcov. = rob_se(ols_mod))
iv_res   <- coeftest(iv_mod,   vcov. = rob_se(iv_mod))

# First-stage F-statistic for instrument relevance
iv_sum   <- summary(iv_mod, diagnostics = TRUE)
first_F  <- iv_sum$diagnostics["Weak instruments", "statistic"]

# -------------------- OUTPUT -------------------- #
cat("===== OLS (baseline) =====\n")
print(ols_res["x", ])

cat("\n===== IV (2SLS) =====\n")
print(iv_res["x", ])

cat("\nFirst-stage F-statistic on instrument (rule-of-thumb ≥10): ",
    round(first_F, 2), "\n")

# -------------------- ROBUSTNESS CHECKS -------------------- #
# 1. Add squared rainfall as an additional instrument (if relevant)
if(!"z2" %in% names(df)){
  df$z2 <- df$z^2
}
iv_mod_alt <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + z2 + controls, data = df)
iv_alt_res <- coeftest(iv_mod_alt, vcov. = rob_se(iv_mod_alt))

cat("\n===== IV with z & z^2 as instruments =====\n")
print(iv_alt_res["x", ])

# Hansen J test for over-identifying restrictions
if(length(iv_mod_alt$instrument) > 1){
  hansenJ <- summary(iv_mod_alt, diagnostics = TRUE)$diagnostics["Sargan",]
  cat("\nHansen J (p-value): ", round(hansenJ["p-value"], 3), "\n")
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Sign: Negative – higher income, induced by positive rainfall, should lower the likelihood of civil conflict (better economic prospects reduce grievances).  
Magnitude: A one-standard-deviation increase in income is anticipated to cut conflict incidence by roughly 0.5 to 1.0 standard deviations (i.e., IV coefficient ≈ –0.5 to –1.0), larger in absolute value than the biased OLS estimate because IV purges attenuation and simultaneity biases.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use rainfall variation as an instrument for income.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Increased income, driven by higher rainfall, reduces the likelihood of civil conflict.
